question: When readers are familiar and sentences are new, does real EEG beat random noise and word-count/timing controls?

split.grouping: Merge sentence keys with identical alphanumeric tokens or token Jaccard >= 0.7
split.train_only: Every group that occurs in both releases
split.strata: Release, then word-count tertile within release

preprocessing.input: Existing 105-channel 200 Hz prepared waveforms; deterministic centered crop to 1600 samples
preprocessing.normalizer: Existing channel normalizer fit on training observations only

ridge.selection: Highest validation primary metric; first grid entry on ties

arms.timing_only_ridge: Observation duration, word count and a training-derived word-count basis; no EEG amplitudes

controls.gaussian: Existing observation/channel-matched noise in training and evaluation
controls.class_shuffled: Existing derangement of training sentence classes; evaluated on real EEG

evaluation.candidate_pool: Validation or test sentences from the query's own release
evaluation.aggregation: Mean within reader, then equal weight across 30 readers
evaluation.primary: Expected 10-way top-1 accuracy with uniform random distractors; chance 10%
secondary: Expected 10-way accuracy among the 20 candidates closest in word count
evaluation.ties: A tie with the correct sentence counts as a miss

gate.scope: Applied separately to ridge and CNN on validation
gate.bootstrap: 10000 resamples; 95% lower bounds above zero for real minus Gaussian when resampling readers and when resampling sentences

test_policy: Score a model and its matched controls once on test sentences only if that model passes the gate; otherwise never score test sentences
stop_rule: Stop after this run whatever the outcome. No extra seeds, settings or architectures under this plan.
existing_output_policy: Refuse to run if the output directory exists; hash protected prior artifacts before and after
